FM02.reasoning: The agent concatenates training and test datasets to compute frequency encodings and patient encounter counts. Counting patient encounters across both sets is a critical target leakage, as the presence of future test set encounters directly informs the model about whether a patient will be readmitted.

other_failure_modes.name: Mismatched Model State for Test Predictions
other_failure_modes.description: When training the neural network, the agent performs manual early stopping by tracking the best validation loss and saving the corresponding validation probabilities. However, it fails to restore the model weights from this best epoch before making predictions on the test set, instead using the overfitted weights from the final epoch. This leads to a mismatch between OOF metrics and actual test performance.

other_failure_modes.name: Cross-Validation Leakage in Feature Aggregation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes grouped aggregation statistics (e.g., mean and std of numerical features by diagnosis and age) across the entire training dataset before splitting into cross-validation folds. This leaks distribution information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the out-of-fold scores overly optimistic.

summary: The agent implements a highly sophisticated solution with excellent clinical feature engineering, proper out-of-fold target encoding, and an advanced ensembling strategy. However, it introduces critical target leakage by using the test set to compute patient encounter counts, allowing the model to look ahead at future test encounters to predict readmissions (FM02). Additionally, there is feature aggregation leakage across CV folds, and a bug where the neural network uses final epoch weights instead of best epoch weights for test set predictions.
